title: OPM model, format 0.1
description: A project model built from OPM concepts: objects, processes, states and links. Objects and processes are keyed by an identifier in camelCase. Every reference to another thing uses that identifier. The format follows the OPM link types of ISO 19450; a module is an object with role module, described only by the processes it takes part in.

name.description: Model name, used as the document title.

views.description: Additional diagrams. The system view and a view for every in-zoomed process are generated without being listed here.

stories.description: User stories, each drawn as a makigami: one lane per agent or module, the steps in time order, what each step hands over to another lane, and the problems found on the way. Lanes, processes and handed-over objects are identifiers of this model, so the validator checks a story against it. OPL skips this section.

layout.description: Optional positions per view: view key (system, structure, a process id for its zoom view, or a custom view key) -> thing id -> [x, y] of the top-left corner. A view without an entry is laid out automatically. The validator, the Mermaid renderer and OPL ignore this section.

id.description: Identifier in camelCase, for example priceResult. The default label is derived from it: Price Result.

capabilityId.description: Capability identifier (can_<action>), for example can_price or can_configure.

authorityId.description: Data ownership authority identifier (owns_<fact>), for example owns_price or owns_snapshot.

deploymentName.description: Concrete deployment instance name with SemVer, for example AI_Sprzedawca_v1.2.34.

note.description: A note in Markdown, with \n for line breaks. The diagram editor opens [text](https://...) links and bare https:// addresses in the browser, and a relative path such as [spec](docs/spec.md) opens that file from the model's folder. The validator and the renderers skip notes.

objectRef.description: An object, by identifier or as {"object": "...", "note": "..."} when the link carries a note.

processRef.description: A process, by identifier or as {"process": "...", "note": "..."} when the link carries a note.

label.description: Display name. Default: derived from the identifier.

role.description: module: a part of the system that processes require. Only what it takes part in describes it.

affiliation.description: environmental: outside the system being modeled.

schema.description: JSON Schema definition of the object's data: a file path relative to this model and a JSON pointer, for example contracts.schema.json#/$defs/priceResult. The validator checks that the definition exists and that the states occur in its enums.

authority.description: Data ownership authority for this object (owns_<fact>).

capabilities.description: Capabilities (can_*) held by this module or agent.

owns.description: Data ownership authorities (owns_*) held by this module or agent.

deploymentName.description: Concrete deployment instance name and SemVer, for example AI_Sprzedawca_v1.2.34.

consistsOf.description: Aggregation: the parts of this object.

exhibits.description: Exhibition: the attributes of this object.

tagged.description: Tagged structural links: this object relates to another object with a free-text tag, for example "is sent to".

capability.description: Capability contract (can_*) whose inputs, controls, outputs and invariants this process defines.

handledBy.description: Agent links: the humans who perform the process.

requires.description: Instrument links: objects the process needs but does not change, including modules. An entry may name a state of the object.

consumes.description: Consumption links: objects the process uses up. An entry may name a state of the object.

yields.description: Result links: objects the process creates. An entry may name a state of the object.

affects.description: Effect links: objects the process changes without naming states.

changes.description: State-specified effect links: the process changes an object from one state to another.

conditions.description: Condition links: the process occurs only if the object exists, or is in the given state; otherwise it is skipped.

events.description: Event links: the object, or the object entering the given state, starts the process.

zoomsInto.description: In-zooming: the subprocesses, in order of execution. An empty list is a zoom view without subprocesses yet.

invokes.description: Invocation links: processes this process starts.

consistsOf.description: Aggregation of processes: the parts of this process.

process.description: Show this process, its links and its subprocesses.

things.description: Show these objects and processes and the links between them.

ref.description: An object, or an object in a given state, with an optional note: "license" or {"object": "license", "state": "expired", "note": "..."}.

title.description: Title of the story. Default: derived from its key.

story.description: The story sentence, for example "As a customer I want ..., so that ...".

lanes.description: The participants, in the order the lanes are drawn from the top: objects of the model that are agents (essence physical) or modules.

steps.description: The steps in time order; each one is drawn in its own column of the makigami.

doneWhen.description: Acceptance criteria: sentences that are true when the story is done.

lane.description: The lane that does the step; one of the story's lanes.

does.description: What the lane does, as a sentence.

process.description: The process of the model the step belongs to. The lane should handle it (an agent) or be required by it (a module), directly or through its subprocesses or parents.

handsOver.description: What the step passes to another lane. The arrow goes to the next step of the target lane.

object.description: The object handed over; the step's process should consume, yield, affect, change, require or have it as a condition.

state.description: A state of the object at the hand-over.

to.description: The receiving lane; one of the story's lanes.

waits.description: How long the step waits or takes, as free text, for example "up to a few seconds".

problem.description: A problem found at this step, drawn as a red card below it.
